content:
Stephanie Nguyen: Brightline Insurance security review came back w/ an evidence ask list. Dropping here so we can triage + commit to dates. They want response within 5 biz days.

Stephanie Nguyen: Context: they’re evaluating Redwood for claims triage + agent assist. They’re leaning Private (VPC) but comparing against “just use managed endpoints in-cloud.” Need to be crisp + not over-claim.

Avery Johnson: +1. They explicitly said their CISO will stall if we don’t show auditability + retention controls.

Stephanie Nguyen: Here’s their ask list (verbatim-ish):
1) SOC 2 Type II report (latest) + bridge letter if report period ended
2) ISO 27001 cert (if any)
3) Pen test summary (last 12 months) + remediation status
4) Data encryption: in transit + at rest; key mgmt options (customer-managed keys?)
5) Audit logs: sample, fields, export options, retention
6) Data retention & deletion policy (including backup retention)
7) Data residency / region controls (esp. US-only)
8) Subprocessors list + notification policy
9) RBAC + SSO/SAML + SCIM support (IdP metadata requirements)
10) Incident response plan summary + breach notification timelines
11) BCP/DR: RTO/RPO targets + test cadence
12) Vulnerability management + patch SLAs
13) Support access controls (how support accesses customer envs)
14) Standard DPA + any GLBA-specific language
15) Product architecture diagram (Private deployment topology)

Stephanie Nguyen: I told them we can share “evidence pack” under NDA, and we’ll send an index today + delivery dates. Naomi/Olga can you confirm what we can send + redaction?

Naomi Feldman: Yep. Please do NOT send the SOC2 PDF in email. We’ll use the secure share flow + watermarking. We can send the evidence pack index openly (no restricted docs).

Olga Petrov: For #1 we can provide SOC2 Type II under NDA via secure link. Bridge letter: I think we have the standard one for Q1—will confirm latest is still valid.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: For #2 ISO: we should be explicit. We’re not ISO certified today. We can share our ISO-aligned controls mapping (internal doc) only if needed; otherwise just say “not currently certified.”

Avery Johnson: :thumbsup: re ISO clarity.

Markus Klein: On #15 architecture diagram: we have the Private (VPC) reference arch slide in the regulated deck + the one-pager diagram draft. I can tailor a customer-facing PNG/PDF that’s safe.

Fatima Noor: For #5 audit logs: I can provide sample payload + explain fields (actor, action, resource, request_id, model, policy decision, etc) + export patterns (S3 / SIEM forward). But we need to confirm what’s GA vs “in progress.”

Vivek Kulkarni: For Private: export options are available but some formats are “supported-by-SE” not self-serve. Let’s phrase carefully: “supported integrations available; roadmap for additional formats.”

Lauren Bishop: For Dedicated (if they consider it): residency controls vary by region; in the meantime they asked US-only so we can commit to US regions for hosted/dedicated, but Private VPC is the cleanest story.

Michael Grant: #14 DPA: we can share standard DPA + subprocessors exhibit. GLBA-specific language usually sits in the customer’s addendum; we can propose our standard + negotiate. Don’t promise “GLBA certified” or similar.

Sofia Mendes: Also #10 breach notification timelines: we should align to our standard contractual language (e.g., “without undue delay” + specific window if negotiated). Don’t commit in Slack/ email—route through Legal.

Stephanie Nguyen: Great. Proposed owners + deadlines (pls react/confirm):
- #1 SOC2 + bridge: Olga + Naomi (secure share). Target: send secure link by Thu EOD.
- #2 ISO answer: Aisha (1 paragraph approved language) by tomorrow 10am.
- #3 Pen test summary: Naomi (redacted exec summary) by Fri EOD.
- #4 Encryption/KMS: Naomi + Vivek (private deployment specifics) by Thu EOD.
- #5 Audit logs sample/schema: Fatima + Vivek review by Fri noon.
- #6 Retention/deletion policy: Naomi (policy statement) + Vivek (Private knobs) by Fri EOD.
- #7 Residency/region controls: Lauren + Vivek (Hosted/Dedicated vs Private) by Thu EOD.
- #8 Subprocessors: Olga (current list) by tomorrow EOD.
- #9 RBAC/SSO/SAML/SCIM: Naomi (security posture) + Fatima (implementation notes) by Fri noon.
- #10 IR plan summary: Naomi by Fri EOD.
- #11 BCP/DR: Naomi by Mon EOD (if we have clean RTO/RPO language).
- #12 Vuln mgmt + patch SLAs: Naomi by Mon EOD.
- #13 Support access controls: Naomi by Mon EOD.
- #14 DPA: Michael + Sofia by Mon EOD (send template under NDA).
- #15 Arch diagram: Markus by Thu noon.

Avery Johnson: Works for me. I can package the response email + track the commitments. Just need the “what we can say” snippets.

Naomi Feldman: Confirmed on secure share. Please route anything “restricted” through me before sending. Also: for #11/#12/#13 we’ll keep it high level unless they request deeper artifacts.

Olga Petrov: Confirmed. I’ll pull the latest SOC2 + subprocessors exhibit. Need the Brightline NDA status—are we covered?

Stephanie Nguyen: NDA is executed as of this morning (Brightline sent countersigned). I’ll DM you the executed PDF + their security portal link.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: I’ll draft ISO language now. Suggested: “Redwood is SOC 2 Type II audited; we are not currently ISO 27001 certified.” No extra color unless asked.

Fatima Noor: For #9: they asked “SCIM support (yes/no)”. We should say: SAML SSO is supported; SCIM is supported for select plans / deployments (confirm). If not, we need to be precise.

Vivek Kulkarni: SCIM is supported for Console user provisioning in enterprise. For Private, depends on the control plane mode. I’ll give you a short matrix.

Markus Klein: I’ll export the Private ref arch (VPC) diagram with labels for: customer VPC, Redwood control plane (if applicable), model runtime nodes, logging sink, KMS integration point. Will avoid any internal infra details.

Sofia Mendes: FYI: If they push for a fixed breach window (e.g., 72 hours), we can negotiate but let’s not pre-commit.

Stephanie Nguyen: :thumbsup: Next step: I’ll send Brightline the evidence pack index today + confirm we’ll deliver items in 2 waves (Thu/Fri) + remainder Monday.

Avery Johnson: Please include that audit log sample will be “representative” and fields may vary by deployment mode/version.

Naomi Feldman: +1, and add the line: “No customer prompts/outputs are included in logs by default; configurable options exist.” (but only if that’s true across modes—Vivek/Fatima please sanity check)

Fatima Noor: Sanity check: by default we log metadata + request IDs; content logging is off unless customer explicitly enables debug. I’ll confirm exact wording.

Stephanie Nguyen: Great. Keeping this thread as the single source of truth for owners/dates. If anything slips, call it early.

Slackbot: Reminder set by Stephanie Nguyen for this thread: “Brightline evidence pack wave 1 due Thu EOD” at 2025-05-08 16:00

Olga Petrov: Update: subprocessors list is current as of last month; includes cloud provider + monitoring vendors. I’ll share the approved customer-facing version.

Markus Klein: Draft arch diagram ready. Sending to Stephanie + Naomi for review (no external share yet).

Naomi Feldman: Reviewed Markus diagram—looks good. One tweak: label audit log export as “customer-owned storage/SIEM” to make boundary clear.

Stephanie Nguyen: Perfect. I’ll send the index + wave 1 ETA now.
